title: Job Scheduler
tagline: A job queue built from scratch: Redis sorted sets, retries with backoff, a dead-letter path, and a live dashboard fed by Redis pub/sub over WebSockets.
author: Chirag Mukhija

walkthrough.title: A job is submitted
walkthrough.body: The API writes the job to Postgres (the durable record), adds its id to a Redis sorted set scored by run time (the fast index of what is due), and publishes job:created for the dashboards.

walkthrough.title: A worker claims work
walkthrough.body: The worker asks Redis for the earliest due job in each of 10 priority tiers, claims it with a guarded UPDATE (WHERE status = 'pending') so two workers can't take the same job, runs one of two handlers picked by job type, then completes it or schedules a retry with backoff.

walkthrough.title: How the dashboard stays live
walkthrough.body: Workers publish events on the Redis channel job:events. The API process subscribes and pushes each event over every open WebSocket, and then every dashboard calls GET /stats again. That last step is what a scale finding flags.

walkthrough.title: The page also polls
walkthrough.body: On top of the live socket, the dashboard re-fetches /stats every 5 seconds.

walkthrough.title: Workers announce themselves
walkthrough.body: Every 5 seconds each worker publishes a heartbeat; the API keeps the last-seen time in memory to show which workers are online.

title: InstaBackend
tagline: An Instagram-style API: JWT auth with Redis sessions, S3 presigned uploads, fan-out feeds and keyset pagination behind Nginx.
author: Chirag Mukhija

walkthrough.title: Signing up
walkthrough.body: Nginx forwards the request and six library middleware run, including a rate limiter that keeps its counters in Redis. The service checks email and username, hashes the password with bcrypt on libuv's thread pool, inserts the user and stores a refresh-token session in Redis.

walkthrough.title: Publishing a post fans it out
walkthrough.body: Creating a post also copies it into every follower's feed (fan-out on write): one query fetches all follower ids with no limit, then one bulk INSERT. Cheap for most users, heavy for someone with a million followers.

walkthrough.title: Reading the precomputed feed
walkthrough.body: This reads the feed_items rows written at post time. Compare it with GET /api/feed/fanout-read, which joins follows and posts on every read instead.

walkthrough.title: Uploads skip the API
walkthrough.body: The server signs an S3 upload URL locally, with no network call at all, and the browser sends the image straight to S3.

walkthrough.title: A profile is four queries
walkthrough.body: Loading a profile runs one lookup, then three COUNT queries in parallel with Promise.all.

title: Payment Gateway
tagline: Idempotent payments on Postgres: API-key auth on every request, and each payment plus its first audit event in one transaction.
author: Chirag Mukhija

walkthrough.title: Creating a payment
walkthrough.body: Auth looks up the merchant by API key on every request. The idempotency key is checked, then the payment and its first audit event are written in one transaction on a dedicated connection: BEGIN, two INSERTs, COMMIT (ROLLBACK on error), and the connection goes back to the pool.

walkthrough.title: Reading a payment
walkthrough.body: Two queries: the payment by id, then its full event history.

walkthrough.title: Listing payments
walkthrough.body: LIMIT/OFFSET pagination capped at 100 rows, served by the (merchant_id, created_at) index from the schema.

title: Hackathon Starter
tagline: A popular Express + MongoDB starter with Passport logins, sessions in MongoDB, email, and dozens of third-party API examples. A big real codebase to explore.
author: Sahat Yalkabov
license: MIT License; code excerpts shown under it

walkthrough.title: Signing up
walkthrough.body: Fifteen middleware run before the handler, including express-session loading the session from MongoDB and Passport loading the user. The handler checks for an existing user, saves the new one, and may email a sign-in link (opening a new SMTP transport for each email).

walkthrough.title: Waiting on someone else's API
walkthrough.body: This request waits on the New York Times API, with no timeout set.

walkthrough.title: Charging a card
walkthrough.body: Stripe is called inside the request, so checkout speed depends on Stripe's.

walkthrough.title: Changing a password
walkthrough.body: isAuthenticated guards the route; the handler loads the user and saves the new password.
